proposals.before: At the beginning of the Hongzhi reign, Wang Shu, seeing that Wen had long been kept in subordinate posts, appointed him left administration commissioner of Shandong.
proposals.after: At the beginning of the Hongzhi reign, Wang Shu, seeing that Wen had long been kept in subordinate posts, appointed him left administration vice commissioner of Shandong.
proposals.reason: 參政 is a vice commissioner post, not 布政使; the next sentence promotes him to left provincial administration commissioner of Yunnan, so Shandong should not already be commissioner.

proposals.before: When Hongzhi changed the reign title, Wang Shu, because Wen had long been held back, employed him as left administration commissioner of Shandong.
proposals.after: When Hongzhi changed the reign title, Wang Shu, because Wen had long been held back, employed him as left administration vice commissioner of Shandong.
proposals.reason: Same office error: 山東左參政 is vice commissioner, not administration commissioner.

proposals.before: As right vice censor-in-chief he pacified Huguang, was transferred to pacify Henan, and was summoned as right vice minister of Revenue.
proposals.after: As right vice censor-in-chief he served as grand coordinator of Huguang, was transferred as grand coordinator of Henan, and was summoned as right vice minister of Revenue.
proposals.reason: 巡撫 here is the Ming grand-coordinator office, not a military pacification.

proposals.before: Han Wen's sons—the Gaotang prefect Han Shicong and Ministry of Justice Director Han Shiji—were both struck from the rolls.
proposals.after: Han Wen's sons—the Gaotang prefect Han Shicong and Ministry of Justice Director Han Shiqi—were both struck from the rolls.
proposals.reason: The given name 士奇 is Shiqi, not Shiji.

proposals.before: Wen's sons—the Gaotang Prefect Shicong and the Ministry of Justice Director Shiji—were both struck from the rolls.
proposals.after: Wen's sons—the Gaotang Prefect Shicong and the Ministry of Justice Director Shiqi—were both struck from the rolls.
proposals.reason: The given name 士奇 is Shiqi, not Shiji.

proposals.before: Shiji was a metropolitan graduate and ended his career as Administrative Commissioner of Huguang.
proposals.after: Shiqi was a metropolitan graduate and ended his career as Administrative Commissioner of Huguang.
proposals.reason: Continues the 士奇 error as Shiji.

proposals.before: Shiji was a metropolitan graduate and ended as Administrative Commissioner of Huguang.
proposals.after: Shiqi was a metropolitan graduate and ended as Administrative Commissioner of Huguang.
proposals.reason: Continues the 士奇 error as Shiji.

proposals.before: Sun Tingwei was a metropolitan graduate and served as acting minister of the Court of the Imperial Stud.
proposals.after: His grandson Tingwei was a metropolitan graduate and served as acting minister of the Court of the Imperial Stud.
proposals.reason: In this Han Wen coda 孫廷瑋 is kinship grandson plus given name Tingwei, not a surname Sun.

proposals.before: Sun Tingwei was a metropolitan graduate and served as Acting Minister of the Court of the Imperial Stud.
proposals.after: Grandson Tingwei was a metropolitan graduate and served as Acting Minister of the Court of the Imperial Stud.
proposals.reason: Literal English likewise treats 孫 as a surname.

proposals.before: During Hongzhi he was twice promoted to Vice Minister of the Court of Judicial Review, then elevated to Right Assistant Censor-in-Chief and appointed Grand Coordinator of Shanxi.
proposals.after: During Hongzhi he was further promoted to Vice Minister of the Court of Judicial Review, then elevated to Right Assistant Censor-in-Chief and appointed Grand Coordinator of Shanxi.
proposals.reason: 再遷 means promoted again (further advanced), not promoted twice into the same Dali vice-ministership.

proposals.before: Jin's intentions slightly eased, yet [Fuhua] was still convicted as a member of Fuhua's villainous faction, and with Shousui and others their names were posted in the court hall.
proposals.after: Jin's intentions slightly eased, yet [Fuhua] was still convicted as a member of the villainous faction, and with Shousui and others their names were posted in the court hall.
proposals.reason: 坐敷華奸黨 means Fuhua was convicted as a factional criminal, not as a member of a faction belonging to Fuhua.

proposals.before: His son Aoshan became a censor.
proposals.after: His grandson Aoshan became a censor.
proposals.reason: 孫 marks a grandson, not a son.

proposals.before: Sun Aoshan—[his] office: censor.
proposals.after: His grandson Aoshan held office as a censor.
proposals.reason: 孫 is kinship 'grandson,' not the surname Sun; 鰲山 is the grandson's given name.

proposals.before: In his sixth year in office he submitted a memorial on six matters, arguing: 'The Prince of Cheng took up the throne in a time of crisis, put down rebellion, and rendered great service to the realm.
proposals.after: In the sixth year [of Chenghua] he submitted a memorial on six matters, arguing: 'The Prince of Cheng took up the throne in a time of crisis, put down rebellion, and rendered great service to the realm.
proposals.reason: After 成化二年, 六年 in this biography is Chenghua 6, not an independent count of years in office.

proposals.before: After his death he was given the posthumous name 'Li,' and public opinion was not fair.
proposals.after: After his death he was given the posthumous name 'Li,' and public opinion was unreconciled.
proposals.reason: 公論不平 means public opinion found the name unjust, not that public opinion itself was unfair.

proposals.before: When Vice Director Sun Guo'an was recalled to office while still in mourning for his mother, Shousui joined Supervising Secretary Li He and others in a series of memorials protesting the appointment, and Sun was finally ordered to resume mourning.
proposals.after: When Vice Director Sun Guang'an was recalled to office while still in mourning for his mother, Shousui joined Supervising Secretary Li He and others in a series of memorials protesting the appointment, and Sun was finally ordered to resume mourning.
proposals.reason: 廣安 is Guang'an, not Guo'an.

proposals.before: Prisoners sent from the Ministry of Punishments for sentence review at the Court often received harsher penalties; Chief Clerk Zhu Zheng protested that this was improper.
proposals.after: Prisoners sent from the Ministry of Punishments for sentence review at the Court often received harsher penalties; Chief Clerk Zhu Cong protested that this was improper.
proposals.reason: 瑽 is Cong, not Zheng.

proposals.before: The Emperor then shelved Zhu Zheng's memorial.
proposals.after: The Emperor then shelved Zhu Cong's memorial.
proposals.reason: 瑽 is Cong; the idiomatic 'Zhu's' already avoids the bad pinyin.

proposals.before: I beg Your Majesty to seize hold of imperial authority, punish these men without delay, heed the lesson of the Yanshi reign, and do not let your servant follow in the doomed footsteps of the eunuchs Fan and Wu.
proposals.after: I beg Your Majesty to seize hold of imperial authority, punish these men without delay, heed the lesson of the Yanxi reign, and do not let your servant follow in the doomed footsteps of Fan and Wu.
proposals.reason: 延熹 is the Eastern Han Yanxi era, not Yanshi; 蕃、武 are Chen Fan and Dou Wu, whose attempt against the eunuchs failed, not eunuchs themselves.

proposals.before: I humbly hope Your Majesty will greatly rouse the imperial authority, immediately impose heavy punishment on this lot, take distant mirror from the error of Yanshi, and do not let your minister tread the already overturned track of Fan and Wu.
proposals.after: I humbly hope Your Majesty will greatly rouse the imperial authority, immediately impose heavy punishment on this lot, take distant mirror from the error of Yanxi, and do not let your minister tread the already overturned track of Fan and Wu.
proposals.reason: 延熹 should be transcribed Yanxi, matching the Eastern Han era name in the Chinese.

proposals.before: When the Earl of Xining, Tan You, arrived with capital reinforcements, the raiders fled.
proposals.after: When the Earl of Xinning, Tan You, arrived with capital reinforcements, the raiders fled.
proposals.reason: 新寧伯 is Earl of Xinning, not Xining (西寧).

proposals.before: The Earl of Xining Tan You came with capital troops as reinforcements, and [they] then fled.
proposals.after: The Earl of Xinning Tan You came with capital troops as reinforcements, and [they] then fled.
proposals.reason: 新寧 should be Xinning, not Xining.

proposals.before: When Liu Jin manipulated power, [Jin] also often went along and indulged his wishes, but Jin was never pleased.
proposals.after: When Liu Jin manipulated power, [Jin] also often went along and indulged his wishes, but Liu Jin was never pleased.
proposals.reason: The subject of 瑾終不悅 is Liu Jin (瑾), not Xu Jin; the literal English wrongly makes Jin the one who was never pleased.

proposals.before: When Jin was supervising the Tuan camp, he served alongside Jin.
proposals.after: When Jin was supervising the Tuan camp, he served alongside Liu Jin.
proposals.reason: 與瑾同事 refers to Liu Jin (瑾). Rendering 瑾 as a second Jin collapses him with Xu Jin.

proposals.before: When Xu Jin ran afoul of Liu Jin and was struck from the rolls, Gao was also demoted to magistrate of Quanzhou.
proposals.after: When Xu Jin ran afoul of Liu Jin and was struck from the rolls, Gao was also demoted to assistant magistrate of Quanzhou.
proposals.reason: 判官 is an assistant magistrate or prefectural judge, not the magistrate (知縣).

proposals.before: He was appointed investigating censor of Daming.
proposals.after: He was appointed prefectural judge of Daming.
proposals.reason: 大名推官 is a prefectural judge, not an investigating censor (御史).

proposals.before: Appointed investigating censor of Daming.
proposals.after: Appointed prefectural judge of Daming.
proposals.reason: Matches 推官; the packet's 'investigating censor' is the wrong office.

proposals.before: One Zhan Cong denounced Vice Minister of Personnel Xu Jin, and the case was referred to Censor-in-Chief Wang Yao for investigation.
proposals.after: One Zhan Cong denounced Vice Minister of Personnel Xu Jing, and the case was referred to Censor-in-Chief Wang Hong for investigation.
proposals.reason: Chinese 徐縉 is Xu Jing, not Xu Jin (許進); 汪鋐 is Wang Hong, not Wang Yao.

proposals.before: There was one Zhan Cong, who denounced Vice Minister of Personnel Xu Jin; the case was sent down to Censor-in-Chief Wang Yao for investigation.
proposals.after: There was one Zhan Cong, who denounced Vice Minister of Personnel Xu Jing; the case was sent down to Censor-in-Chief Wang Hong for investigation.
proposals.reason: Same 徐縉/汪鋐 mistranslations as in the idiomatic field.

proposals.before: Zhan Cong was left speechless under questioning and had already been found guilty, yet he again denounced Xu Jin, Assistant Director of Transmission Chen Jing, and others.
proposals.after: Zhan Cong was left speechless under questioning and had already been found guilty, yet he again denounced Xu Jing, Assistant Director of Transmission Chen Jing, and others.
proposals.reason: 縉 continues 徐縉 (Xu Jing), not 許進.

proposals.before: The case was again referred to Wang Yao for investigation, and Wang forcefully rejected the charges as false.
proposals.after: The case was again referred to Wang Hong for investigation, and Wang forcefully rejected the charges as false.
proposals.reason: 鋐 is Wang Hong (汪鋐), not Wang Yao.

proposals.before: The case was again sent down to Wang Yao for investigation, and Yao forcefully rejected his charges as false.
proposals.after: The case was again sent down to Wang Hong for investigation, and Hong forcefully rejected his charges as false.
proposals.reason: 汪鋐 / 鋐 should be Wang Hong, not Yao.

proposals.before: Meanwhile Minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices Peng Ze wished to bring down Xu Jin and take his place. He forged a letter in Xu's name to Zhang Fuxing seeking exoneration, then incited Fuxing to impeach Xu for having bribed him.
proposals.after: Meanwhile Minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices Peng Ze wished to bring down Xu Jing and take his place. He forged a letter in Xu's name to Zhang Fujing seeking exoneration, then incited Fujing to impeach Xu for having bribed him.
proposals.reason: 徐縉 is Xu Jing; 張孚敬 is Zhang Fujing, not Zhang Fuxing.

proposals.before: Xu Jin submitted a memorial in his own defense, and an edict ordered the judicial offices to investigate jointly with the Embroidered Uniform Guard.
proposals.after: Xu Jing submitted a memorial in his own defense, and an edict ordered the judicial offices to investigate jointly with the Embroidered Uniform Guard.
proposals.reason: 縉 remains Xu Jing (徐縉).

proposals.before: Zan and the others finally found Zhan Cong guilty of false accusation, but Xu Jin's alleged bribery could not be cleared, and he was dismissed from office.
proposals.after: Zan and the others finally found Zhan Cong guilty of false accusation, but Xu Jing's alleged bribery could not be cleared, and he was dismissed from office.
proposals.reason: 縉 is Xu Jing, not Xu Jin.

proposals.before: He was appointed investigating censor of Shunde, then entered the capital as a secretary in the Ministry of War before being transferred to the Ministry of Rites.
proposals.after: He was appointed judge of Shunde, then entered the capital as a secretary in the Ministry of War before being transferred to the Ministry of Rites.
proposals.reason: 順德推官 is the prefectural judge of Shunde, not an investigating censor.

proposals.before: Appointed investigating censor of Shunde, he entered the capital as a secretary in the Ministry of War and was changed to the Ministry of Rites.
proposals.after: Appointed judge of Shunde, he entered the capital as a secretary in the Ministry of War and was changed to the Ministry of Rites.
proposals.reason: The literal line repeats the same mistranslation of 推官 as investigating censor.

proposals.before: When the court recommended candidates for Censor-in-Chief of Shuntian, Lun's name ranked second.
proposals.after: When the court recommended candidates for Grand Coordinator of Shuntian, Lun's name ranked second.
proposals.reason: 順天巡撫 is the grand coordinator of Shuntian, not Censor-in-Chief.

proposals.before: When the court recommended candidates for Censor-in-Chief of Shuntian, Lun's name ranked second.
proposals.after: When the court recommended candidates for Grand Coordinator of Shuntian, Lun's name ranked second.
proposals.reason: The literal English likewise renders 巡撫 as Censor-in-Chief.

proposals.before: The emperor said, "That is the one who submitted the Treatise on the Nine Border Regions Illustrated," and immediately appointed him Right Vice Censor-in-Chief and assigned him the post.
proposals.after: The emperor said, "That is the one who submitted the Treatise on the Nine Border Regions Illustrated," and immediately appointed him Right Assistant Censor-in-Chief and assigned him the post.
proposals.reason: 右僉都御史 is Right Assistant Censor-in-Chief; 副都御史 is the vice rank.

proposals.before: His merit was recorded and he was promoted to Right Assistant Censor-in-Chief.
proposals.after: His merit was recorded and he was promoted to Right Vice Censor-in-Chief.
proposals.reason: 右副都御史 is Right Vice Censor-in-Chief, not Assistant (僉都).

proposals.before: His merit was recorded and he was promoted to Right Assistant Censor-in-Chief.
proposals.after: His merit was recorded and he was promoted to Right Vice Censor-in-Chief.
proposals.reason: The literal English also swaps 副都御史 for the assistant rank.

proposals.before: When he arrived he was broken by guerrilla officer Hu Zhen.
proposals.after: When they arrived they were broken by guerrilla officer Hu Zhen.
proposals.reason: The subject of 至則 is the raiders of the previous sentence, not a single person being defeated.

proposals.before: Removed to magistrate of Wu County.
proposals.after: Appointed magistrate of Wu County.
proposals.reason: The verb 除 here is appointment to office, not removal.

proposals.before: Deputy commander Wang Jie had committed an offense; Tai impeached him and was himself ordered down for questioning.
proposals.after: Deputy commander Wang Jie had committed an offense; Tai impeached him and Jie was sent down to Tai to be arrested and questioned.
proposals.reason: 下泰逮問 means the accused was sent to Tai for arrest and interrogation, not that Tai was himself sent down.

proposals.before: Deputy commander Wang Jie had a crime; Tai impeached him; Tai was sent down for arrest and questioning.
proposals.after: Deputy commander Wang Jie had a crime; Tai impeached him; Jie was sent down to Tai for arrest and questioning.
proposals.reason: Same reversal of 下泰逮問 as in the idiomatic translation.

proposals.before: Late Chenghua advanced scholar; removed to magistrate of Jianyang.
proposals.after: Late Chenghua advanced scholar; appointed magistrate of Jianyang.
proposals.reason: 除 here means appointment to office, not removal; 'removed to' reverses the sense.

proposals.before: Sat because he once recommended Tai; compelled to commoner.
proposals.after: Charged because he once recommended Tai; compelled to commoner status.
proposals.reason: 坐 marks conviction or implication, not the verb 'to sit'.

proposals.before: In the fourth year he was transferred to magistrate of the Capital Prefecture.
proposals.after: In the fourth year he was transferred to Prefectural Governor (Yin) of Yingtian.
proposals.reason: 應天府尹 is the Yin of Yingtian (Nanjing), not a generic Capital Prefecture magistrate; the idiomatic rendering drops the place-name.

proposals.before: Fan fled to the capital to accuse Xiu; the emperor sent down both Xiu to the clerks, demoted to prefect of Qingfeng; Fan and Jin also had their names removed.
proposals.after: Fan fled to the capital to accuse Xiu; the emperor sent both Xiu and Fan down to the judicial clerks; Xiu was demoted to magistrate of Qingfeng; Fan and Jin also had their names removed.
proposals.reason: 知清豐 is a county magistracy, not a prefecture; the literal also drops 並's second object after 下繡吏.

proposals.before: In the second year, together with Regional Commander Ma Rui, the Earl Who Pacified the Qiang, he campaigned and pacified the Zhuang of Hexian.
proposals.after: In the second year, together with Regional Commander Ma Rui, Earl of Fuqiang, he campaigned and pacified the Zhuang of Hexian.
proposals.reason: 伏羌伯 is the Earl of Fuqiang (a toponymic peerage), not Earl Who Pacified the Qiang.

proposals.before: Fan exhorted Jun to cease hostilities, but Jun refused; Fan then joined Garrison Supervisor Wei Jing and Regional Commander Ma Rui, the Earl Who Pacified the Qiang, mustering more than a hundred thousand troops in six columns to attack.
proposals.after: Fan exhorted Jun to cease hostilities, but Jun refused; Fan then joined Garrison Supervisor Wei Jing and Regional Commander Mao Rui, Earl of Fuqiang, mustering more than a hundred thousand troops in six columns to attack.
proposals.reason: Chinese 毛銳 is Mao Rui, not Ma Rui, and 伏羌伯 is the territorial earldom of Fuqiang rather than who pacified the Qiang.

proposals.before: Fan exhorted Jun to cease hostilities; he refused, so Fan joined Garrison Supervisor Wei Jing and Regional Commander Ma Rui, Earl Who Pacified the Qiang, gathering more than a hundred thousand troops in six columns to attack.
proposals.after: Fan exhorted Jun to cease hostilities; he refused, so Fan joined Garrison Supervisor Wei Jing and Regional Commander Mao Rui, Earl of Fuqiang, gathering more than a hundred thousand troops in six columns to attack.
proposals.reason: The literal line repeats the same two errors in 毛銳 and 伏羌伯.

proposals.before: Fu Nan She besieged Danzhou; Hu Fu and Participant Liu Xin went to reconnoiter.
proposals.after: Fu Nan She besieged Danzhou; Hu Fu and Administration Vice Commissioner Liu Xin went to reconnoiter.
proposals.reason: Ming 參議 is an administration vice commissioner, not the office Participant.

proposals.before: When the bandits Aben and others of Shizong Prefecture rebelled, persuasion failed; he then sent Administration Commissioner Chen Yijing and others to lead twenty thousand troops against them, while another force blocked the Pan River and took the bandits' lair from the rear; more than a thousand were captured or killed in all.
proposals.after: When the bandits Aben and others of Shizong Prefecture rebelled, persuasion failed; he then sent Administration Vice Commissioner Chen Yijing and others to lead twenty thousand troops against them, while another force blocked the Pan River and took the bandits' lair from the rear; more than a thousand were captured or killed in all.
proposals.reason: 參議 is an administration vice commissioner, not the higher office implied by Administration Commissioner.

proposals.before: When Minister of Works Li Yong retired, the court nominated Wendu and Nanjing Vice Minister of Revenue Wang Heng; Wendu was then made Nanjing Minister of Revenue, and both he and Heng were forced to retire.
proposals.after: When Minister of Works Li Sui retired, the court nominated Wendu and Nanjing Vice Minister of Revenue Wang Heng; Wendu was then made Nanjing Minister of Revenue, and both he and Heng were forced to retire.
proposals.reason: 李鐩 is Li Sui; idiomatic Li Yong misreads the given name.

proposals.before: Later Chen Jin entered the Censorate as Left Censor-in-Chief with the title Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent, ranking above Jing; people nicknamed Jing the "Central Capital Censor."
proposals.after: Later Chen Jin entered the Censorate as Left Censor-in-Chief with the title Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent, ranking above Jing; people nicknamed Jing the "Middle Censor-in-Chief."
proposals.reason: 中都御史 here means the middle of the three censors, not the Central Capital; Chen Jin ranked above Jing and Zhang Lun held the right post.

proposals.before: An edict declared that dismissed officials would not be prosecuted; both Jing and Nai were spared.
proposals.after: An edict declared that dismissed officials would not be prosecuted; both Jing and Quan were spared.
proposals.reason: Chinese 銓 is Gao Quan, not Zhang Nai; the English wrongly reused Nai.

proposals.before: An edict ordered that those who had left office not be prosecuted; Jing and Nai were both pardoned.
proposals.after: An edict ordered that those who had left office not be prosecuted; Jing and Quan were both pardoned.
proposals.reason: Chinese 銓 is Gao Quan; literal English mistakenly has Nai.

proposals.before: Nai came from Jiangdu and eventually served as minister of Revenue at Nanjing.
proposals.after: Quan came from Jiangdu and eventually served as minister of Revenue at Nanjing.
proposals.reason: The subject is 銓 (Gao Quan), not Zhang Nai.

proposals.before: Nai was a native of Jiangdu and rose through offices to minister of Revenue at Nanjing.
proposals.after: Quan was a native of Jiangdu and rose through offices to minister of Revenue at Nanjing.
proposals.reason: The subject is 銓 (Gao Quan), not Zhang Nai.

proposals.before: As Jin grew harsher, his investigators usually sought severity to please him, and both Fang and Nai were caught up in the prosecutions.
proposals.after: As Jin grew harsher, his investigators usually sought severity to please him, and both Fang and Quan were caught up in the prosecutions.
proposals.reason: Chinese 銓 is Gao Quan, not Zhang Nai.

proposals.before: Later Jin grew still more harsh in control; each time he sent envoys to investigate, most strove for severity to please Jin, and Fang and Nai were both among those impeached.
proposals.after: Later Jin grew still more harsh in control; each time he sent envoys to investigate, most strove for severity to please Jin, and Fang and Quan were both among those impeached.
proposals.reason: Chinese 銓 is Gao Quan, not Zhang Nai.

proposals.before: After Jin was executed, Nai was restored to office, retired, and died.
proposals.after: After Jin was executed, Quan was restored to office, retired, and died.
proposals.reason: Chinese 銓 is Gao Quan, not Zhang Nai.

proposals.before: When Jin was executed, Nai was restored to office and retired, then died.
proposals.after: When Jin was executed, Quan was restored to office and retired, then died.
proposals.reason: Chinese 銓 is Gao Quan, not Zhang Nai.

proposals.before: He was again prosecuted for assigning corvée laborers to serve at Minister Qin Xian's household while grand coordinator of Shandong.
proposals.after: He was again prosecuted for assigning corvée laborers to serve at Minister Qin Hong's household while grand coordinator of Shandong.
proposals.reason: The personal name 秦纮 is Qin Hong (Hong), not Qin Xian; Xian does not match 纮.

proposals.before: Again, while pacifying Shandong he had used corvée laborers to serve at the home of Minister Qin Xian, and once more the touring censor was ordered to arrest and question him.
proposals.after: Again, while pacifying Shandong he had used corvée laborers to serve at the home of Minister Qin Hong, and once more the touring censor was ordered to arrest and question him.
proposals.reason: The personal name 秦纮 is Qin Hong, not Qin Xian.

decisions.reason: Chinese 山東左參政 is the provincial administration vice-commissioner post; 布政使 appears only in the next unit as Yunnan left provincial administration commissioner.
The literal line repeats the same office error: 山東左參政 is vice commissioner, not administration commissioner.
巡撫湖廣 and 移撫河南 name the Ming grand-coordinator office, not a campaign of pacification.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 以右副都御史巡撫湖廣，移撫河南

decisions.after: Han Wen's sons—the Gaotang prefect Han Shicong and Ministry of Justice secretary Han Shiqi—were both struck from the rolls.
decisions.reason: 士奇 is Shiqi, not Shiji; 刑部主事 is a secretary, not a director (郎中).

decisions.after: Wen's sons—the Gaotang Prefect Shicong and the Ministry of Justice secretary Shiqi—were both struck from the rolls.
decisions.reason: 士奇 is Shiqi, not Shiji; 主事 should not be rendered Director.

decisions.after: Shiqi was a metropolitan graduate and ended his career as Administration Vice Commissioner of Huguang.
decisions.reason: 士奇 is Shiqi, not Shiji; 湖廣參政 is an administration vice commissioner, not a provincial administration commissioner (布政使).

decisions.after: Shiqi was a metropolitan graduate and ended as Administration Vice Commissioner of Huguang.
decisions.reason: The literal line keeps Shiji and also over-ranks 參政 as Administrative Commissioner.
In this Han Wen family coda 孫 is kinship 'grandson' plus given name 廷瑋, not a surname Sun.
The literal English likewise treats 孫 as a surname rather than 'grandson'.
After the Hejian prefecture posting, 再遷大理少卿 means he was next advanced to that office, not twice appointed to it.
坐敷華奸黨 convicts Fuhua as a factional criminal; it does not make the faction Fuhua's own.
孫鰲山 marks Zhang Fuhua's grandson Aoshan, not a son.
孫 is kinship 'grandson,' not the surname Sun; 鰲山 is the grandson's given name.
After 成化二年, 六年 continues the Chenghua year count; it is not a sixth year in office.

decisions.after: After his death he was given the posthumous name 'Li,' and public opinion found it unjust.
decisions.reason: 公論不平 means the public judged the posthumous name unjust, not that public opinion itself was unfair; 'unreconciled' is awkward.
廣安 is Guang'an; Guo'an does not match the given name.
朱瑽 is Cong, not Zheng.
帝乃瑽寢奏 refers to Zhu Cong (瑽), not Zhu Zheng.
延熹 is the Eastern Han Yanxi era; 蕃、武 are Chen Fan and Dou Wu, anti-eunuch ministers, not eunuchs.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 遠鑒延熹之失，毋使臣蹈蕃、武已覆之轍

decisions.reason: 延熹 should be transcribed Yanxi, matching the era name.
新寧伯 is Earl of Xinning, not Xining (西寧).
新寧 is Xinning, not Xining.
The subject of 瑾終不悅 is Liu Jin (瑾), not Xu Jin.
與瑾同事 refers to Liu Jin; a second 'Jin' collapses him with Xu Jin.
全州判官 is an assistant magistrate or prefectural judge, not the magistrate (知縣).
大名推官 is a prefectural judgeship; 召拜御史 in the next sentence is the later censorate appointment.
The literal line repeats the mistranslation of 推官 as investigating censor.
徐縉 is Xu Jing, distinct from 許進; 汪鋐 is Wang Hong, not Wang Yao.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 訐吏部侍郎徐縉，下都御史汪鋐訊

decisions.reason: The literal line has the same 徐縉 / 汪鋐 name errors.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 吏部侍郎徐縉，下都御史汪鋐訊

decisions.reason: 縉 continues 徐縉 (Xu Jing), not 許進.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 摐復訐縉及通政陳經等

decisions.reason: 鋐 is Wang Hong (汪鋐), not Wang Yao.
汪鋐 / 鋐 should be Wang Hong throughout the literal sentence.
縉 is Xu Jing; 張孚敬 is Zhang Fujing, not Zhang Fuxing.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 欲傾縉代之，偽為縉書抵張孚敬

decisions.reason: 縉 remains Xu Jing (徐縉).
而縉行賄事莫能白 still refers to Xu Jing, not Xu Jin.
順德推官 is the prefectural judge of Shunde, not an investigating censor.
The literal line repeats the mistranslation of 推官 as investigating censor.
順天巡撫 is the grand coordinator of Shuntian; the 右僉都御史 appointment follows in the next sentence.
The literal English likewise renders 巡撫 as Censor-in-Chief.
右僉都御史 is Right Assistant Censor-in-Chief; 副都御史 is the vice rank.
右副都御史 is Right Vice Censor-in-Chief, not Assistant (僉都).
The literal English also swaps 副都御史 for the assistant rank.
至則 continues the raiders of the previous sentence (把都兒), not a single person arriving to be defeated.
除吳縣知縣 uses 除 as appointment to office, not removal.
下泰逮問 sends the impeached officer down to Tai for arrest and interrogation, not Tai himself.
The literal line reverses the same 下泰逮問 construction.
除建陽知縣 is an appointment; 'removed to' reverses 除.
坐 marks implication or conviction, not the verb 'to sit'.
應天府尹 is the Yin of Yingtian, not a generic capital-prefecture magistracy, and the place-name must be kept.
知清豐 is a county magistracy, not a prefecture; 並下繡吏 also sends Fan with Xiu to the clerks, as 璠、進亦除名 then names Fan's further penalty.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 帝並下繡吏，謫知清豐，璠、進亦除名

decisions.after: In the second year, together with Regional Commander Mao Rui, Earl of Fuqiang, he campaigned and pacified the Zhuang of Hexian.
decisions.reason: 伏羌伯 is the toponymic earldom of Fuqiang, but 毛銳 is Mao Rui, not Ma Rui; the proposal left the wrong surname.
毛銳 is Mao Rui and 伏羌伯 is Earl of Fuqiang, not Ma Rui or a descriptive 'Earl Who Pacified the Qiang'.
The literal line repeats the same errors in 毛銳 and 伏羌伯.

decisions.after: Fu Nan She besieged Danzhou; Hu Fu and Assistant Administration Commissioner Liu Xin went to reconnoiter.
decisions.reason: 參議 is not the calque 'Participant,' but it is also below 參政: assistant administration commissioner, not administration vice commissioner.

decisions.after: When the bandits Aben and others of Shizong Prefecture rebelled, persuasion failed; he then sent Assistant Administration Commissioner Chen Yijing and others to lead twenty thousand troops against them, while another force blocked the Pan River and took the bandits' lair from the rear; more than a thousand were captured or killed in all.
decisions.reason: 參議 is below both 布政使 and 參政; 'Administration Vice Commissioner' still over-ranks Chen Yijing.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 乃遣參議陳一經等督軍二萬攻之

decisions.reason: 李鐩 is Li Sui; Yong does not match 鐩.
With Chen Jin ranking above Jing and Zhang Lun as right censor-in-chief, 中都御史 is the middle of the three censors, not the Central Capital.
璟、銓並獲免 names Gao Quan (銓), not Zhang Nai.
The literal line likewise substitutes Nai for 銓 (Gao Quan).
The subject of 銓，江都人 is Gao Quan, not Zhang Nai.
The literal subject is likewise 銓 (Gao Quan).
淓遂並銓在劾中 keeps 銓 as Gao Quan, not Zhang Nai.
The literal English repeats Nai for 銓.
銓復官致仕 is Gao Quan after Liu Jin's execution, not Zhang Nai.
The literal line repeats Nai for 銓.
秦纮 is Qin Hong; Xian does not match 纮.
The literal personal name 秦纮 is Qin Hong, not Qin Xian.

claimRetractions.reason: The personal-name Sun Tingwei exists only because English treated kinship 孫 as a surname; the unit supports given name Tingwei and grandsonhood, already extracted separately.

claimRevisions.reason: The English personal name Shiji was produced only by misreading 士奇; the source given name is Shiqi.
湖廣參政 is an administration vice-commissioner post, not a provincial administration commissioner.

Metropolitan graduate ending as Administration Vice Commissioner of Huguang.

claimRevisions.reason: The attestation event copied the over-ranked English office title for 參政.
The English Guo'an was created by misreading 廣安; the source name is Guang'an.
The English Zheng was created by misreading 瑽; the source name is Cong.
毛銳 is Mao Rui; English Ma Rui treats 毛 as if it were 馬.
參議 is the assistant administration commissioner, one rank below 參政.
The office label over-ranks 參議 as a vice commissioner.
The English Yong was created by misreading 鐩; the source name is Sui.
中都御史 in this anecdote is the middle of three censors-in-chief, not a Central Capital title.
The English Xian was created by misreading 纮; the source name is Hong.
